questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Under no circumstances should the funds be transferred without approval.
Under no circumstances the funds should be transferred without approval.
Under no circumstances the funds be transferred should without approval.
Under no circumstances should the funds transferred be without approval.
questions.explanation: 'Under no circumstances' triggers inversion: 'should the funds be transferred.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: It is imperative that the data be verified before publication.
It is imperative that the data is verified before publication.
It is imperative that the data will be verified before publication.
It is imperative that the data being verified before publication.
questions.explanation: After 'it is imperative that', the subjunctive is used: 'the data be verified.'

questions.topic: Advanced conditionals (If it were not for)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If it were not for strong exports, the economy would be in recession.
If it was not for strong exports, the economy would be in recession.
If it were not for strong exports, the economy will be in recession.
If it not were for strong exports, the economy would be in recession.
questions.explanation: 'If it were not for' expresses a hypothetical present condition: 'the economy would be in recession.'

questions.topic: Concession connectors (even though vs even if)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Even though profits fell, the company maintained its dividend.
Even if profits fell, the company maintained its dividend.
Even though profits falling, the company maintained its dividend.
Even though profits fell, but the company maintained its dividend.
questions.explanation: 'Even though' introduces a real, factual concession: 'Even though profits fell...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: All the manager did was postpone the inevitable decision.
All the manager did was postponing the inevitable decision.
All that did the manager was postpone the inevitable decision.
All the manager was doing postpone the inevitable decision.
questions.explanation: 'All...did was + base verb' is a common cleft structure: 'All the manager did was postpone...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The CEO conceded that the launch had been mismanaged.
The CEO conceded to that the launch had been mismanaged.
The CEO conceded the launch being mismanaged.
The CEO is concede that the launch had been mismanaged.
questions.explanation: 'Concede' is followed by 'that + clause': 'conceded that the launch had been mismanaged.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Faced with mounting debt, the firm filed for restructuring.
Face with mounting debt, the firm filed for restructuring.
Facing with mounting debt, the firm filed for restructuring.
Faced with mounting debt, the firm filing for restructuring.
questions.explanation: 'Faced with' is a past participle clause meaning 'confronted by': 'Faced with mounting debt, the firm filed...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A plethora of options has left customers confused.
A plethora of options have left customers confused.
A plethora of options is leaving customers confused already.
A plethora options have left customers confused.
questions.explanation: 'A plethora of' + plural noun typically takes a plural verb: 'a plethora of options have left customers confused.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The startup might have survived with better funding.
The startup might survived with better funding.
The startup might have survive with better funding.
The startup might have surviving with better funding.
questions.explanation: 'Might have + past participle' expresses a past possibility: 'might have survived with better funding.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Whether the deal goes through or not, the reputational damage is done.
Whether the deal goes through or not that, the reputational damage is done.
Whether does the deal go through or not, the reputational damage is done.
Whether the deal going through or not, the reputational damage is done.
questions.explanation: 'Whether...or not' introduces a concessive clause: 'Whether the deal goes through or not...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The policy could conceivably backfire if implemented too quickly.
The policy could conceivable backfire if implemented too quickly.
The policy conceivably could backfiring if implemented too quickly.
The policy could backfire conceivably it if implemented too quickly.
questions.explanation: 'Conceivably' hedges a claim and sits after the modal: 'could conceivably backfire.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm returned to the market whence its early success had come.
The firm returned to the market where its early success had come from whence.
The firm returned to the market whence that its early success had come.
The firm returned to the market from whence its early success had came.
questions.explanation: 'Whence' is a formal, literary relative adverb meaning 'from which': 'the market whence its early success had come.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Not until the audit was finalized was the fraud confirmed.
Not until the audit was finalized the fraud was confirmed.
Not until the audit finalized was the fraud confirmed.
Not until the audit was finalized the fraud confirmed was.
questions.explanation: Fronting 'not until' triggers inversion: 'Not until the audit was finalized was the fraud confirmed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The postponement of the launch disappointed investors.
The postpone of the launch disappointed investors.
The postponement of the launch disappoint investors.
The postponing the launch disappointed investors.
questions.explanation: Formal writing nominalizes verbs: 'postpone' becomes 'the postponement of...'

questions.topic: Passive with modal perfect (would have been)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The project would have been completed on time if not for the strike.
The project would been completed on time if not for the strike.
The project would have completed on time if not for the strike.
The project would have being completed on time if not for the strike.
questions.explanation: Modal perfect passive: modal + have been + past participle: 'would have been completed.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: One region reported growth; the other, stagnation.
One region reported growth; the other reported, stagnation.
One region reported growth; the other is stagnation.
One region reported growth; the other reports stagnation already.
questions.explanation: Ellipsis omits the repeated verb after a semicolon: 'the other, stagnation' (= the other reported stagnation).

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Demand collapsed overnight. As a result, prices were slashed.
Demand collapsed overnight, as a result prices were slashed.
Demand collapsed overnight. As a result prices were slashed.
Demand collapsed overnight as a result, prices were slashed.
questions.explanation: 'As a result' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Regardless of the risks, the board approved the expansion.
Regardless the risks, the board approved the expansion.
Regardless of the risks, but the board approved the expansion.
The risks regardless of, the board approved the expansion.
questions.explanation: 'Regardless of' is followed directly by a noun phrase: 'Regardless of the risks...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email declining a business offer?
options: Nah, we're gonna pass on this one.
Thank you for your proposal; however, we have decided not to proceed at this time.
Not interested, sorry.
We'll pass, but thanks for reaching out I guess.
questions.explanation: 'Thank you for your proposal; however, we have decided not to proceed...' is a standard polite, formal decline.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about a faulty product?
options: I am writing to bring to your attention a defect in a product purchased from your company.
This product is broken and I want my money back now.
I am writing to bring to your attention a defect in a product purchased from your company, yeah.
Your product doesn't work and that's unacceptable.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use precise, measured language such as 'I am writing to bring to your attention...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company decided to branch out into international markets.
The company decided to branch the international markets out into.
The company decided to branch out of into international markets.
The company decided to branch international markets out into.
questions.explanation: 'Branch out' means 'to expand into new areas': 'branch out into international markets.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The company had its license revoked after the investigation.
The company had its license revoke after the investigation.
The company had revoked its license after the investigation.
The company had its license revoking after the investigation.
questions.explanation: 'Have + object + past participle' shows something happening to the subject: 'had its license revoked.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Given the circumstances, the decision seems reasonable.
Give the circumstances, the decision seems reasonable.
Giving the circumstances, the decision seems reasonable.
Given the circumstances that, the decision seems reasonable.
questions.explanation: 'Given the circumstances' is a fixed absolute participle phrase meaning 'considering the circumstances.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By virtue of its size, the firm can negotiate lower prices.
By virtue its size, the firm can negotiate lower prices.
By the virtue of its size, the firm can negotiate lower prices, that.
Virtue of its size, the firm can negotiate lower prices.
questions.explanation: 'By virtue of' means 'because of': 'By virtue of its size, the firm can negotiate...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The startup managed to raise capital from several venture funds.
The startup managed to lift capital from several venture funds.
The startup managed to grow capital raise from several venture funds.
The startup managed to raise of capital from several venture funds.
questions.explanation: 'Raise capital' is a fixed collocation: 'the startup managed to raise capital.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The firm has gradually reduced its reliance on fossil fuels.
The firm has reduced gradually its reliance on fossil fuels.
Gradually the firm has reduced its reliance on fossil fuels.
The firm gradually has reduced its reliance on fossil fuels.
questions.explanation: Adverbs of manner typically follow the auxiliary verb: 'has gradually reduced.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Costs remain high. That said, margins have improved.
Costs remain high, that said margins have improved.
Costs remain high. That said margins have improved.
Costs remain high that said, margins have improved.
questions.explanation: 'That said' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma.

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: The auditors would barely notice such a small discrepancy, would they?
The auditors would barely notice such a small discrepancy, wouldn't they?
The auditors would barely notice such a small discrepancy, don't they?
The auditors would barely notice such a small discrepancy, do they?
questions.explanation: 'Barely' makes the statement effectively negative, so the tag is positive: 'would barely notice..., would they?'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The forecast was not entirely accurate.
The forecast was not all accurate entirely.
The forecast not was entirely accurate.
The forecast was entirely not accurate.
questions.explanation: Formal understatement places 'not' before the adverb: 'was not entirely accurate.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Had the board known of the risks, it would have vetoed the deal.
Had the board know of the risks, it would have vetoed the deal.
The board had known of the risks, it would have vetoed the deal.
Had the board known of the risks, it will have vetoed the deal.
questions.explanation: 'Had + subject + past participle' is an inverted third conditional: 'Had the board known..., it would have vetoed...'
